title: Events, Retreats and Gatherings | R&SVP – Hio Ridge, Bridgton, Maine
description: A barn on 22 acres in Bridgton, Maine, for showers, reunions, retreats, teas, small concerts, workshops and classes. Up to 135 guests. Tables and chairs included.
heading: Events and gatherings
lede: Any kind of an event. Showers, reunions, retreats, teas, birthday and retirement parties, small concerts, and the papercrafting classes we hold in the barn ourselves.
hero_alt: The barn with round tables set on the patio, lawn in front

kinds.title: Baby and wedding showers
kinds.body: Round tables in the barn, the patio for the afternoon, and the field for photos.

kinds.title: Reunions and parties
kinds.body: Family reunions, birthdays, retirement parties and anniversaries. Up to 135 people, with your caterer in the prep kitchen.

kinds.title: Retreats
kinds.body: Women's retreats, church groups, and company retreats. The barn for the sessions, the patio and the field for the breaks, and the Lakes Region for the evenings.

kinds.title: Small concerts
kinds.body: The acoustics in the barn are good. The High Street Jazz Band played our open house. We would love a bluegrass, country or gospel group next. [CONFIRM: band name]

kinds.title: Teas and workshops
kinds.body: Afternoon teas, creative workshops and classes. We have 15 seats at the tables for a class.

kinds.title: Community events
kinds.body: Once a year we donate the venue for a charitable event. If you have one in mind, ask.

classes.heading: Cardmaking in the barn
classes.body: Susan teaches papercrafting and cardmaking classes in the barn. You make five cards or items at each class, and all supplies are provided. Watch our Facebook page for dates.
classes.alt: Guests beside the stone planter at the barn on a fall afternoon
classes.caption: Fall Cards and Venue Views, October 2026

upcoming_empty: No events are scheduled right now. Follow us on Facebook, or ask about hosting your own.

retreats.heading: Retreats for parents
retreats.body: Susan spent her career in special education, and she is the mother of a daughter with autism. She knows how hard the first years can be. She is planning retreats here for parents of children with disabilities: a weekend at the barn with a guest speaker, time to meet other parents, and a reason to come back each year. [CONFIRM: ready to announce]

closing.heading: Tell us about your event
closing.body: The date, about how many people, and what you have in mind. We will get back to you with what the barn can do.
